name: Grease and Glory
description: Escort Brother Ashmaw and his blessed charge across the Boiling Floor to the mud-throat.
briefing: Sled-log. Ashmaw wants the mud-throat. That is the big vent at the middle of the Boiling Floor, the one that never stops coughing. He says one charge down its neck will open a grease seam that will keep the kilns running for ten years, and he says it the way other people say grace.

He goes himself. Powder-Monks do not let anyone else carry a blessed charge, and this one has a name. I asked what the name was. He said it was "Patience", which I think was a joke, but with Ashmaw you cannot tell.

The scouts say something is walking up the far side of the rift, slow and bronze, carrying a light. Ashmaw says it is a pilgrim. I say a pilgrim does not need a ridge of Bell-Knights. Get him to the throat. Get him back if we can.
victoryText: Ashmaw kneels in the boiling mud, says the charge's name, and drops it down the throat. The floor heaves. Grease wells up black and sweet, and a column of fire stands over the rift for an hour. Across it, the bronze priest stops and watches, and lifts her small flame toward the column, as if greeting a relative. Then she walks on, up toward the sky.
defeatText: The Court closes over the throat like water over a dropped stone. Ashmaw is carried home on a sled, scalded and humming. "Next year," he says. Nobody argues. Nobody wants to go back.

victory.label: Get Brother Ashmaw to the mud-throat

do.speaker: Brother Ashmaw
do.text: Mind the vents. They boil anyone not born under a mile of water. That is most of us. Ah. All of us.

do.speaker: Scout
do.text: The Court comes up through the floor, on the vents.

do.speaker: Maelis Quell
do.text: We carry a flame to the open sky, small one. You are standing on its chimney.

condition.label: Let the flame pass: Maelis Quell survives
